control.name: CONTROL — stop refusing an SSH push url under a bot identity (the whole fault: the push goes out under a human's key while the commits read as the App's)

mutations.name: read remote.<name>.url and ignore pushurl (the fetch-url-only reading the fault hides behind: `remote -v`'s first line looks clean)
check only the FIRST push url (a push fans out to every pushurl, so a clean first value is not a pass)
round a failed git-config read up to a pass (could-not-check reported as 'no SSH found, carry on')
round a remote with NO url at all up to a pass (nothing was examined, so nothing can have been cleared)
treat the scp-like `git@host:path` shorthand as not-SSH (the spelling every house checkout actually carries)
swallow the https-without-an-App-credential-helper NOTICE (the ambient-identity shape one layer along, reported as silence)
swallow the unresolvable-$DESK_LOOP NOTICE by making the gate speak for every session (over-application: a human with no App identity is gated too)
deskpr create no longer runs the push-transport gate (the wiring, not the gate: a correct gate nobody calls)
deskpr update no longer runs the push-transport gate
deskwt add no longer runs the push-transport gate (every worktree it cuts inherits the SSH remote unchallenged)
